Their structures were elucidated on the basis of comprehensive spectroscopic studies including IR, MS, and 1H, 13C,2DNMRspectra.Compound3isanewcompoundin nature, andcompounds 4–6have been isolatedforthe first timefromR.japonica.Theisolateswereevaluatedfortheir antibacterial activity against three strains (43504, 51, and AtifAliKhanKhalil,WooSungParkandJeehoonLeehave contributedequallytothiswork.

The four isolated juglone derivatives(1–4)showedpotentgrowthinhibitoryactivity.

Amongthem,compounds1–3exhibitedstrongerinhibitory activity than those of the positive controls, juglone and metronidazole, for the three strains and that of another reference, clarithromycin, for the 43504 and 51 strains.

Specifically, the new juglone compound 3 displayed the most potent antibacterial activity against all three strains, 43504, 51, and 26695, with MIC values of 0.06, 0.06 and 0.13 lM,respectively,andMIC valuesof0.14,0.11and 0.15 lM, respectively.

Keywords Reynoutria japonica (cid:2) Juglone derivatives (cid:2) Anti-Helicobacter pylori activity Introduction The medicinal plant Reynoutria japonica Houtt. (Polygonum cuspidatum Siebold & Zucc.) is a Japanese knotweedwhichbelongstotheplantfamilyPolygonaceae.Itis a native perennial herb that is 1–2 m tall and is largely availableinSouthKorea,Japan,China,NorthAmericaand Europe (Shan et al. 2008; Patocka et al. It is a rich source of functional metabolites, and its delicate stem has beenutilizedindaily foodstuffs(Kirinoetal.20,while its roots have been used as a coloring agent for rice.

Furthermore, the root of this plant has been traditionally used as herbal medicine in the treatment of inflammation, infection, jaundice, skin burns, chronic bronchitis and hyperlipidemia diseases in the form of granules, powders and decoctions (Peng et al. A large number of secondary metabolites have been isolated from this plant including quinones, stilbenes, flavonoids, coumarins and other polyphenolic compounds, and these functionally important phytochemicals are known to have anti-inflammatory, anticancer, antiviral and antibacterial activities (Peng et al. 2013; Patocka et al. Naphthoquinones are secondary metabolites found in plants and possess a variety of interesting biological properties.

Many of the 1,4-naphthoquinones, especially 5-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinones (juglone) and its derivatives, exhibit potent biological activities including antibacterial,antifungal,antiviral(Tandonetal.2004;Ryu and Chae 2005; Park et al. 2006; Kim et al. 20, antiplatelet (Son et al. 20, antidiabetic (Shah et al. 20, antitumor(Jiaweietal.20andcytotoxiceffects(Inbaraj and Chignell 2004; Phutdhawong et al. 2012; Jin et al. 2016; Manickam et al. Naturally derived 1,4naphthoquinonesorcloselyrelatedchemicalsubstancesare knowntobeusedasantibioticsorchemotherapeuticagents (Omuraetal.1976;BauchandLeistner1980;Tandonetal.

Our previous work reported the chemical structures and anti-Helicobacter pylori activity of five anthraquinones, two stilbenes and a 1,4-naphthoquinone derivative from the root part of R. japonica (Khalil et al. Among the isolates, the juglone, 2-methoxy-6-acetyl-7methyljuglone exhibited the prominent antibacterial activity as a natural compound.

The inhibitory potency was the greatestamongthereportedjuglonederivatives.Therefore, the current study focused on the isolation of another promising anti-H. pylori juglone derivative from R. japonica and on the elucidation of their chemical structures.

Anti-H. pylori activity All isolated compounds (1–9) were analyzed for their antibacterial activity against H. pylori.

Minimal inhibitory concentrations (MICs) were determined for three strains (43504,51,and266ofH.pyloriwiththebrothdilution methodaccordingtoastandardliteratureprocedure(Amin et al. The four isolated juglone derivatives (1–4) showedpotentgrowthinhibitoryactivity(Table 2).Among them,compounds1–3exhibitedstrongerinhibitoryactivity compared to the positive controls, juglone and metronidazoleforthethreestrainsandcomparedtoanotherreference clarithromycin for the 43504 and 51 strains.

Natural substances and their metabolites with less adverse effects are alternative approaches for the intervention of gastric disorders caused by this bacterium.

Naphthoquinones from the medicinal plants are well known for their antibacterial properties including anti-H. pyloriactivityofjugloneanditssyntheticderivatives(Park etal.2006;Sreelathaetal.20.Juglonederivativeshave also shown selective growth inhibition activity against intestinal microflora (Kim et al. The anti-H. pylori activityofjuglonewithahydroxylgroupatC-5(5-hydroxy- 1,4-naphthoquinone)isknowntoshowstrongeractivitythan 1,4-naphthoquione (Park et al. The additional hydroxyl group at C-8 in naphthazalin (5,8-dihydroxy-1,4naphthoquinone) reduced the inhibitory activity, and a methylgroupattheC-2positioninplumbagin(2-methyl-5hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone) increased the inhibitory activity (Park et al. In the present study, all four juglone derivatives among the compounds (1–9) isolated from R. japonica roots showed potent growth inhibitory activity against three strains of H. pylori.
They were 2-methoxy-6-acetyl-7-methyljuglone (1), 2-ethoxy-6acetyl-7-methyljuglone (2), 2-methoxy-7-acetonyljuglone (3) and 7-methoxy-2-methyljuglone (4).

These four compoundscouldbesynthesizedfromR.japonicaviatheacetate-polymalonatepathway,oneofbiosyntheticpathwaysfor plant1,4-naphthoquinones(Steynetal.1970;Widhalmand Rhodes20.Theiranti-H.pyloriactivityshowedthatthe additionofvariousfunctionalgroupstothejugloneskeleton affects growth inhibitory activity.
Compound 2 with an ethoxy group at the C-2 position exhibited slightly more potent activity for strains 51 and 26695 than compound 1 with a methoxy group at the same position.

The additional alkoxygroupatC-2,acetylgroupatC-6andmethylgroupat C-7 of 1 and 2 increased the inhibitory activity approximately5-30timescomparedtojuglone.Specifically,anovel compound 3 having a characteristic acetonyl group at C-7 withamethoxygroupatC-2showedthemostpotentanti-H. pylori activity among the isolates, which were A.A.K.Khaliletal. approximately 20-fold more potent than commercially available clarithromycin, and approximately 40-fold more potentthanjuglone.ThepresenceofanacetylgroupatC-3 and a methoxy group at C-7 in compound 4 decreased the inhibitoryactivityagainstallthreestrains.Theanti-bacterial activitiesofthreejuglonederivatives1–3werestrongerthan that of plumbagin which is known to be the most potent juglonederivative.
Theanti-H.pyloriactionmechanismsincludeinhibition ofbacterialenzymessuchasureaseandN-acetyltansferase, anti-adhesion, oxidative stress to H. pylori, and hydrophilic/hydrophobic interaction (Wang 20.

It is known that juglone inhibits growth of H. pylori via inhibition of three key enzymes cystathionine c-synthase, malonyl- CoA:acyl carrier protein transacylase and b-hydroxyacyl- ACP dehydratase (Kong et al. In addition, juglone acts as a strong, time and concentration dependent inactivator of urease (Kot et al. 2-Methoxy-1,4-naphthoquinoneproducesahighamountofreactiveoxygenspecies to cause damage to H. pylori (Wang et al. Inconclusion,wehaveisolatedanewjuglonederivative withthreeknownjugloneswithpotentantibacterialactivity against Helicobacter pylori.
The new compound was named 2-methoxy-7-acetonyljuglone and was the most potent among the isolates.
These findings suggest that the juglone derivatives isolated from the root of R. japonica may be useful candidates for the eradication of H. pylori infection.
Further studies are required to determine their exactmechanismsofactionandtheireffectsonthehuman body with safety issues.
